intro.data: Three machines in your toolkit. One doesn't even fit — its input port wants a chart, not a CSV (check the type on its tray card). Of the two that fit, only one actually produces the clean table. Bring the right one onto the board and wire it; leave the rest in the tray.
intro.alchemy: Three apparatuses in your toolkit. One doesn't fit — its input wants a tool, not ore. Of the two that fit, only one produces the pure ingot. Bring the right one onto the board; leave the rest in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: Three runes in your toolkit. One doesn't fit — its input wants a beacon, not a spark. Of the two that fit, only one produces the steady flame. Bring the right one onto the board; leave the rest in the tray.
intro.abstract: Three machines in the toolkit. h has the wrong source type (C → B). Of the type-valid A → B machines, f sends a ↦ b and g sends a ↦ b′ — place and wire the one that yields the goal value b.

afterSuccess.data: The Importer never fit — its input port wanted a chart, not a CSV. Between the two that did fit, only the Parser produced a clean table. Type tells you what can connect; behavior tells you what it does.
afterSuccess.alchemy: The Caster never fit — it wanted a tool, not ore. Of the two that fit, only the Smelter made a pure ingot. Type says what connects; behavior says what it does.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: The Binder never fit — it wanted a beacon, not a spark. Of the two that fit, only Ignition made a steady flame. Type says what connects; behavior says what it does.
afterSuccess.abstract: The wrong-typed machine couldn't connect; of the type-valid ones, only one produced the goal. Type is necessary but not sufficient.

reveal.summary: Machines have typed input and output ports: only matching types connect. But among machines that fit, behavior still decides the result.
notation: h: C → B  (won't accept an A)
reveal.moreFormal: A morphism only applies to its source type — that's what the port colors enforce. Two morphisms A → B are both applicable, yet need not agree.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: A function expecting C won't take an A (a type error); two A→B functions can still differ.
